skill.name: global-conventions
skill.description: Apply project-wide conventions for repository structure, Git workflows, documentation, environment settings, dependencies, feature flags, and team collaboration.
skill.summary: Guide assistants to apply shared development conventions across repository and workflow tasks.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The path traversal finding is confirmed because SKILL.md directs the assistant to read a fixed parent-directory path outside the skill folder. The .env detection is a false positive in context because it only lists secrets management as a usage scenario and does not request disclosure. No prompt injection or additional semantic risk was found.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the conventions document inside the skill directory or inline the required guidance in SKILL.md.
Add explicit wording that assistants must never print, copy, store, or transmit secret values from .env or config files.

static_findings.snippet: - When working with .env files, config files, or secrets management

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 29 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/conventions.md and line 28 directs the assistant to use it. This fixed parent-directory reference crosses the skill package boundary and could cause unintended filesystem access or missing-policy behavior.

SKILL.md line 16 only lists .env files, config files, and secrets management as contexts for applying conventions. It does not instruct the assistant to read, reveal, store, or transmit secret values.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when project structure, Git workflows, and documentation rules vary between contributors. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code apply consistent global conventions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when project-wide conventions should guide file organization and directory structure.
Guides commit message, branch, and pull request workflow decisions.
Applies documentation expectations for README files, changelogs, release notes, and contribution guides.
Supports consistent handling of environment settings, dependency files, feature flags, and configuration toggles.
Directs the assistant to a shared conventions reference for detailed standards.
limitations: The skill mostly delegates details to a linked conventions document outside SKILL.md.
It does not include automated validation, linting, or policy enforcement scripts.
It does not define concrete rules for every language, framework, or repository layout.
It should not be used to reveal secrets from .env files or configuration stores.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Setup
use_cases.description: Apply consistent folder, dependency, configuration, and documentation patterns when starting or reorganizing a project.

use_cases.title: Prepare Consistent Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check branch, commit, changelog, and review expectations before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Document Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Create clear setup, contribution, release, and review guidance that follows shared team conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a New Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-conventions to propose a consistent directory structure for this project. Explain the purpose of each top-level folder.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-conventions to review my branch, commit message, documentation updates, and pull request checklist for consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Review Configuration Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-conventions to review changes to environment settings, dependency files, feature flags, and documentation. Do not expose secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Team Workflow Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-conventions to audit our branching, dependency, documentation, review, and release process. Identify gaps and propose a team-ready workflow.

output_examples.input: I need a structure for a new service.
output: Create separate areas for source code, tests, documentation, configuration, and release notes.
Name each top-level folder by purpose and keep generated files out of version control.
Add setup and contribution notes before the first handoff.

output_examples.input: Review my pull request plan for consistency.
output_examples.output: The response would check branch naming, commit clarity, changelog needs, documentation updates, dependency notes, and merge readiness.
The response would document variable names, purposes, and setup steps while keeping secret values private.

best_practices: Keep the linked conventions document available in the repository before relying on this skill.
Ask for concrete checks when applying conventions to commits, branches, documentation, or dependencies.
Treat secret values as private and document only variable names, purposes, and safe setup steps.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a substitute for automated tests, linters, or repository policy checks.
Pasting secret values from .env files into prompts or documentation.
Expecting detailed rules when the linked conventions file is missing or unavailable.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply project-wide conventions for structure, Git workflows, documentation, configuration, dependencies, reviews, and releases.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance unless the user asks the assistant to edit files in the workspace.

faq.question: Can it handle .env files?
faq.answer: It can guide safe environment documentation, but secret values should stay private.

faq.question: Why does it reference another conventions file?
faq.answer: The skill delegates detailed standards to a shared document. That file must be present for full guidance.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for all repositories?
faq.answer: It is best for teams that already maintain shared project conventions. Adapt the guidance for each repository.
